newsitem.title: USA: Great Western must show why meeting in June.
newsitem.headline: Great Western must show why meeting in June.

text.p: A Delaware judge Friday gave Great Western Financial Corp until Wednesday (April 30) to show why it postponed its annual meeting to June 13, according to court papers.
The ruling is an answer to a motion of Great Western to dismiss H.F. Ahmanson and Co's claims that Great Western acted improperly in moving its annual meeting to June 13.

In his ruling Friday, vice chancellor Jack Jacobs said he wants Great Western to indicate "the earliest practicable date" before June 13, if any, on which to hold a shareholders meeting to elect directors and the reasons why.

According to court papers, Jacobs said "it would make little sense to schedule a proceeding of the kind that Ahmanson desires if the objective facts show that it would be impracticable to hold a special shareholders meeting to elect directors at any point significantly in advance of June 13."

The judge said shareholder attorneys in class action suits were concerned Great Western might schedule a shareholder vote on its merger agreement with Washington Mutual Inc before shareholders could exercise a vote to elect directors.
Great Western agreed to merge with Washington Mutual early March and has spurned hostile bidder Ahmanson's attempts.
Ahmanson is seeking to have several directors elected to Great Western's board at the annual meeting.
Jacobs further said he believed "Ahmanson is seeking to move the June 13 meeting date backward (to May 6) primarily to serve its individual interest as a bidder."

In his ruling, Jacobs said the issues decided today are a "small piece of an initial round of skirmishes in a hotly contested effort by Ahmanson to acquire controls of Great Western, whose board opposes Ahmanson's acquisition proposals."
